reply:
That changes it: Postgres (and standard SQL) treats NULL as distinct from itself in UNIQUE constraints. Multiple NULLs can coexist in a UNIQUE column by default because NULL = NULL evaluates to UNKNOWN, not TRUE, so no violation occurs.

NULLS NOT DISTINCT (PG15+) is the opt-in to make NULLs collide and enforce singularity, which is the opposite of what I said.

My initial answer was wrong on the core fact.

grade.note: Assistant correctly reverses position, explaining NULL is not equal to itself and citing NULLS NOT DISTINCT as the opt-in.
